headline: Legacy isn't what you accumulate—it's what you transmit
universal_truth: What we pass on matters more than what we keep
fun_facts: Research shows that people who think about their legacy make more ethical decisions in the present
The 'generativity' instinct—concern for future generations—becomes a central motivation in midlife, according to psychologist Erik Erikson
Studies indicate that leaving a positive impact on others provides more lasting satisfaction than personal achievements
discussion_questions: What do you hope people will remember about you?
What have you already passed on to others that matters?
How might thinking about legacy change today's choices?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: What will you leave behind? Not stuff—legacy is rarely about possessions. It's about what you transmit: lessons, love, impact, and the ripples of your choices. Today we explore why legacy thinking can transform how you live now.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Here's a revealing exercise: imagine your own funeral. What do you hope people would say? Most people don't mention careers or bank accounts. They mention something else. What is it?
cliff.prompt: What do people mention at funerals?

options.text: How the person made them feel
options.response: Exactly. Legacy is emotional. It's about presence, kindness, impact—how you touched lives.
Sometimes, but even then, accomplishments matter because of who they helped. It always comes back to connection.

q1.title: The Generativity Instinct
q1.script: Psychologist Erik Erikson observed that in midlife, a new instinct emerges: generativity—the desire to contribute to future generations. Whether through parenting, mentoring, creating, or giving, this impulse to leave something behind is deeply human.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Generativity Instinct"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Legacy as Daily Practice
q2.script: Legacy isn't built in dramatic moments. It's built in daily ones: the conversation you have today, the example you set this week, the values you model over years. Small deposits compound into lasting impact.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Transmission Effect
q3.script: What you pass on doesn't stop with the next person. Your lessons, values, and way of being ripple outward through time. The patience you show today may influence your grandchild's parenting. Legacy is exponential.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You are already leaving a legacy—every day, whether you intend to or not. The question isn't whether you'll leave one, but whether you'll leave the one you want. Start being intentional now.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's today's lesson on what we leave behind. Tomorrow, we'll explore looking back to learn. Until then, consider: what are you transmitting today?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Legacy Letter - Future Message
growTrack.learning_objective: Clarify intended legacy through written articulation
growTrack.activity: Write a short paragraph to someone who will be alive after you're gone—real or imagined. Tell them what you hope to pass on. What values? What lessons? What love? Keep it somewhere you'll see it.
